text: Plague came to Edinburgh in 1645, and killed a great many people in these crowded closes.
The story of victims bricked up alive is a later legend. The truth is sad enough without extra ghosts.
A heavy table with a candle stub and a clay pipe. Somebody has been through here recently, and not in the 1600s.
Under the pipe is a pouch of coins, most of them very old and very small.
A chest of old household things: pewter, a cracked jug, a lump of fuel the Close once burned.
The Close was cold. Edinburgh in winter has never been polite.
